title: Introduce Budget Marshal: mini-scheduler, quota-sipper, and quant-compat deprecation policy
author: Priya Banerjee
description: Motivation: Many tenants run with conservative batching/caching defaults that waste budget on short interactive flows. This PR introduces the Budget Marshal subsystem: a lightweight tenant-aware mini-scheduler plus a quota-sipper admission controller and a quant-compat deprecation policy to automate safe, unit-economics-driven defaults. Goals are to reduce per-token cost for interactive workloads, provide safe automated rollouts of compact quant profiles, and surface unit-econ signals for ops and product to tune tenant defaults. Summary of changes: 1) mini-scheduler service: a low-latency scheduler that runs in the prefilling path and groups short, affinity-friendly requests into micro-lanes. It supports policy knobs for max-lane-wait-ms, tenant-priority, and cost-target-per-token. 2) quota-sipper admission controller: enforces a soft quota budget per-session that preferentially routes requests into cheaper lanes (microbatch + prefix-caching) when the tenant is on a budget tier. It exposes an API for console overrides. 3) quant-compat deprecation policy: catalog metadata and rollout rules for quant profiles (q4/q8/q6) including a compatibility probe stage, safety rollback thresholds (quality regression > 2% on eval set) and automatic fallback to higher-precision variants. 4) unit-econ telemetry tags: emits token-cost-estimate, lane-type, and prefill-hit-rate tags to tracing and metrics; a new telemetry bridge aggregates per-tenant daily unit-econ snapshots. 5) CLI and defaults-as-code: add budget-marshal CLI that can dry-run tenant defaults and export recommended compact quant profiles as a policy bundle. 6) Tests and canary: synthetic microbench harness plus perf canary job to verify latency and unit-econ regression tolerances. Backwards compatibility and safety: default behavior is opt-in via tenant flag budget_marshal.enabled=false; quant deprecation requires explicit linear ticket and approval to enable for a tenant. The quota-sipper uses soft quotas with graceful degradation — requests never get dropped by the subsystem itself, only routed to non-compact lanes when budgets are exhausted. Rollout plan: staged canary on internal staging tenants, then 5% production traffic with monitoring dashboard and automated rollback if unit-econ delta or latency p95 increases beyond configured thresholds. Checklist: - [x] mini-scheduler core impl - [x] admission controller + API - [x] telemetry tags + bridge - [x] CLI + policy export - [x] unit/e2e tests and perf canary - [x] docs and console feature flag - [x] Linear tickets linked Related work: builds on ENG-1732 (prefill cache API), borrows tracer semantics from ENG-1987 (telemetry bridge), and complements ENG-2123 (tenant defaults CLI). How to test locally: run ./dev/mini_sched --simulate-profile small-interactive and run the canary harness scripts in tools/prefill-sim/ README contains sample commands and expected metrics. Small snippet of policy bundle (example): {"budget_target": "0.002/token", "preferred_quant": "q4_0", "compat_probe_percent": "10"}
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial mini-scheduler implementation, add quota-sipper admission controller, quant-compat metadata and policy engine, telemetry bridge and tags, CLI and docs
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Overall design looks solid. A few concerns: scheduler fairness across tenants and memory pressure when micro-lanes accumulate — please add a per-node lane-cap and eviction policy.
Priya Banerjee (author): Added per-node lane-cap (config: max_lanes_per_node) and an LRU eviction hook; updated tests to cover eviction behavior.
María Alvarez: Telemetry tags look good but make sure token-cost-estimate uses same cost table as billing to avoid discrepancies.
Priya Banerjee: Telemetry bridge now reads cost rates from billing/cost-table and emits cost_version tag so we can audit mismatches.
Jordan Li: Quant-compat rollback threshold seems strict; recommend exposing as tenant override. Also run the compact quant on a tiny human evaluation set before full rollout.
Priya Banerjee: Rollout plan updated to require small human eval for compat_probe stage and tenant override for rollback thresholds.
María Alvarez: CI flaky test on telemetry bridge fixed by increasing test timeout and using stable time source.
checks: perf-canary: passed (latency p50 within 5% of baseline, unit-econ -12% cost)
release_notes: Introduce Budget Marshal mini-scheduler, quota-sipper admission controller, quant-compat deprecation policy, unit-econ telemetry tags, and a CLI for defaults-as-code. Opt-in per-tenant; safe rollout with canaries and automatic rollback conditions.
